claims.text: Decision differences across sensitive groups can be explainable by non-sensitive explanatory attributes.
Existing discrimination-aware techniques introduce reverse discrimination when decision differences across sensitive groups are explainable by other attributes.
Local techniques can be developed to handle conditional discrimination when an attribute is considered explanatory.

evidence.description: Analysis of conditional non-discrimination showing that part of decision differences across sensitive groups can be explainable by attributes like education level.
Observation during classifier design analysis that existing discrimination-aware methods remove explainable differences, thereby introducing reverse discrimination.
Development and experimental evaluation of local techniques for conditional discrimination removal.

methodologies.name: Local techniques for conditional discrimination
methodologies.description: A classifier training approach designed to remove unexplainable discrimination while allowing decision differences that are explainable by a designated explanatory attribute.
conditions: Presence of a sensitive attribute in historical training data
Availability of an attribute designated as explanatory

limitations.text: Existing discrimination-aware techniques aim at removing all discrimination and fail to account for explainable discrimination attributable to other attributes.
